dedupe_keys.name: bundeswaldinventur german national forest inventory results database

description: The Bundeswaldinventur is the German national forest inventory, a terrestrial sample survey first run for reunified Germany in 2002 and repeated for the reference years 2012 and 2022. Survey teams recorded data in 2021 and 2022 at almost 80,000 sample points on a 4 by 4 kilometre grid, denser in some states, capturing more than 150 attributes such as tree species, diameter, height, forest structure and deadwood. The results database at bwi.info makes all data from the inventories since 2002 freely accessible: it stores more than 800 million results, from which about eight million different tables can be built, and results can also be shown as charts or maps, with learning videos and step-by-step guides. Access is free and public; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: results come as tables built online from sample-based estimates, the pages are in German, and bwi.info failed a certificate check from the cloud session. Coverage is Germany. It supports green infrastructure assessment, storm and drought damage studies of forests next to power lines, roads and railways, and climate adaptation; related records are the WEHAM forest development model and the National Forest Inventory of Great Britain.
